A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same frequency-domain change-point detection and selective-inference work. All 30 pages of each version, including appendices, equations and figures, support comparison despite the revised title and organization.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-data experiments on error control, power, runtime and robustness, plus analyses of the IMS bearing dataset.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds a penalty-parameter sensitivity study in Appendix D.4.

M1.justification: Both versions use STFT, dynamic-programming initialization, simulated annealing and parametric-programming selective inference. The logarithmic Metropolis rule in v2 is equivalent to v1's acceptance rule; simplified notation and explicit uniform sampling do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Synthetic signal and noise scenarios and the IMS bearing dataset remain unchanged, including the four bearings and analyzed periods. The new penalty sweep varies a method parameter within existing coverage.

E2.justification: Synthetic error-rate comparisons retain OC, OptSeg-SI-oc, OptSeg-SI, Naive and Bonferroni. Power comparisons retain OC and Bonferroni, and bearing analyses retain OC and Naive. The sensitivity study introduces no new comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix D.4 adds a sweep over κ = 1.0, 1.5, 2.0 and 2.5, using T = 60 for error-rate experiments and Δ = 0.08 for power, with both window sizes. The existing principal experimental settings remain; expanded bearing-data descriptions do not establish a changed protocol.

E4.justification: v2 adds a focused sensitivity analysis testing how the heuristically chosen penalty γ affects error control and power. Existing noise-robustness analyses, runtime analysis and supplementary bearing cases are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the stated 1000-trial principal simulations, 10000 correlated-noise trials and fixed algorithm seed. No new confidence intervals, error bars or uncertainty-estimation practices are introduced.

E6.justification: v2 Figures 14–15 add error-rate and power results across κ, showing higher power for Proposed than OC and Bonferroni and increasing power with κ particularly at M = 512. The matched principal, robustness, runtime and bearing results are retained; these are additional results, not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: v2 Eq. (14) adds an explicit quadratic-form derivation of the projection-norm test statistic that v1 Eq. (12) stated directly. The truncated-χ distribution and conditional/unconditional p-value validity were already present in v1; their reorganization into revised theorem statements does not introduce a new guarantee.

C1.justification: Despite retitling and the new 'Our contribution' paragraph, both versions claim valid selective p-values for frequency-domain CPs shared across frequencies. Both locate the contribution in statistical inference rather than the dynamic-programming/simulated-annealing selector.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 adds an explanation of why directly extending dynamic programming cannot optimize the coupled objective. Appendix D.4 interprets increasing power through stronger penalties selecting clearer changes. The Gaussian-noise limitation is emphasized in the conclusion but was already documented in v1.

D1.justification: v2 specifies uniform neighborhood sampling and expands the bearing-data instructions, explicitly identifying 513 DFT frequency components, the 131 used components and the reference settings for other parameters. It also updates the printed implementation-repository address. These are documentation changes, without demonstrated changes to the retained experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds Loftus and Taylor (2015) to support nuisance conditioning in Section 4.2. The broader related-work coverage and positioning of the contribution remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The central selective-inference exposition in Section 4 is substantially rewritten, simplifying CP indexing and reorganizing hypotheses, statistics and theorem statements. v2 also introduces a dedicated contribution paragraph, expands the real-data explanation, revises the conclusion and systematically replaces anomaly terminology with change-point terminology.

P2.justification: v2 adds two sensitivity figures, removes v1's redundant pipeline schematic in Figure 2, and rearranges the runtime plots into a larger 2-by-2 display. Other figures are principally resized, relabeled or relocated, with expanded captions and a reformatted author block.

improvement.justification: The new sensitivity study addresses a previously unexamined heuristic penalty choice. Clearer inference notation, expanded bearing-data instructions and more readable runtime plots improve exposition and reproducibility. The method, principal evidence and known noise-related limitations remain essentially unchanged, so the overall gains are incremental.
